name: A Survey of Context Engineering for Large Language Models
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2507.13334) [cs.CL]. Submitted 17 Jul 2025 (v1), last revised 21 Jul 2025 (v2). Marked 'ongoing work; 166 pages, 1411 citations'. No peer-reviewed venue found as of the survey date; arXiv-only.
authors_affiliation: Lingrui Mei (lead, corresponding contact), Jiayu Yao, Yuyao Ge, Baolong Bi, Jiazhi Liu, Mingyu Li, Jiafeng Guo, Shenghua Liu (corresponding) - Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences (ICT, CAS) and University of Chinese Academy of Sciences (UCAS); also Key Laboratory of Network Data Science and Technology (ICT, CAS) and State Key Laboratory of AI Safety. Co-authors: Yiwei Wang (University of California, Merced), Yujun Cai (The University of Queensland), Zhong-Zhi Li, Duzhen Zhang, Tianze Xia (UCAS), Chenlin Zhou (Peking University), Jiayi Mao (Tsinghua University). Primary affiliation: ICT, Chinese Academy of Sciences. Contact: meilingrui25b@ict.ac.cn, liushenghua@ict.ac.cn.
code_url: N/A (no method code; this is a survey). The associated curated paper list is the maintained_repo below.
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/Meirtz/Awesome-Context-Engineering (the authors' continuously-updated 'Awesome Context Engineering' curated list, ~3.2k stars; actively maintained and as of March 2026 expanded beyond the frozen PDF to cover agent harnesses, runtime memory, protocols MCP/A2A/AG-UI/ACP/ANP, coding agents, and observability - therefore more current than the July 2025 PDF).
task_domain: Survey / taxonomy spanning the full LLM 'context engineering' landscape: prompt-based generation, in-context learning / CoT reasoning, external knowledge acquisition and RAG (QA, multi-hop, graph), long-sequence processing, self-refinement, structured-information (knowledge-graph) integration, memory systems, tool-integrated reasoning / function calling, and multi-agent systems. Not a single task; it unifies QA, reasoning, tool-use, agentic, and decision-making settings under one framework.
problem_setting: This is a horizontal survey (not a method paper). It formalizes 'Context Engineering' as the systematic optimization of the information payload C supplied to an autoregressive LLM at inference, decomposing C into a set of structured components (instructions, knowledge, tools, memory, state, query) assembled by formatting/concatenation functions, and framing the goal as maximizing expected output quality subject to a context-length budget |C| <= L_max (an information-theoretic / optimization view replacing the single static prompt string with a dynamic, multi-component stream). It covers offline and interactive, single- and multi-agent regimes. Supervision varies by surveyed method (none/frozen prompting, SFT, RL). The survey analyzes over 1400 research papers and is organized into Foundational Components (Context Retrieval & Generation; Context Processing; Context Management) and System Implementations (RAG; Memory Systems; Tool-Integrated Reasoning; Multi-Agent Systems), plus Evaluation and Future Directions. It contributes no new method or experiments of its own.
what_is_retrieved: Survey-level: covers retrieval/acquisition of all major context types - retrieved documents/knowledge (RAG), knowledge-graph subgraphs/structured data, demonstrations/exemplars (ICL/CoT), tools/APIs (tool-integrated reasoning), and memory entries (episodic/long-term agent memory). The survey treats 'context retrieval and generation' broadly: both retrieving external knowledge and generating context (prompts, CoT).
retrieval_grounding: HYBRID (survey-wide). The taxonomy explicitly spans STATIC external corpora/KBs/APIs (classic RAG, knowledge-graph integration, tool documentation) and GROWING/episodic agent memory the system writes (Memory Systems section: MemoryBank, MemGPT, A-MEM, memory hierarchies, persistent interactions). Tool-integrated reasoning and multi-agent memory add further hybrid grounding.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Survey-level synthesis rather than a single objective. It discusses classic top-k retrieval/ranking (RAG, ICL demonstration selection), context-budget-constrained optimal selection (its formal C* = argmax under |C|<=L_max), compression/optimization to fit budgets, and multi-tool/multi-agent coordination where completeness of the needed component set matters. No single completeness-vs-topk metric is its own contribution. [uncertain]
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A. The survey is not a case-based-reasoning method; it does not implement Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain itself. (It catalogs memory and experience-reuse systems, but CBR cycle coverage is a per-method property not applicable to the survey.) [N/A]
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The survey does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not center Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it frames the field as 'Context Engineering' (retrieval/generation, processing, management) integrated into RAG/memory/tool/multi-agent systems.
retrieval_unit: Survey-level: the taxonomy spans many retrievable units - token/snippet and document (RAG), demonstration/exemplar (ICL/CoT), knowledge-graph subgraph and structured records (GraphRAG/KG integration, e.g. HippoRAG, LightRAG, RAPTOR), tool/API specifications (Toolformer, Gorilla, ToolLLM, function-calling), and memory entries (MemoryBank, MemGPT, A-MEM). No single retrieval unit; it is a multi-granularity catalog.
index_source: Survey-wide HYBRID: it reviews static offline-built corpora/KBs and tool registries as well as online/test-time-growing agent memory (memory hierarchies, persistent storage written during interaction). Construction is described as both offline-induced (document indices, KG construction in graph-RAG) and online (memory write-back in agent memory systems).
index_structure_topology: Survey-level: covers flat vector indices (modular RAG), knowledge/dependency GRAPH indices (Graph-Enhanced RAG, GraphRAG, LightRAG, HippoRAG, RAPTOR hierarchical trees), hierarchical memory structures (MemGPT/OS-style memory hierarchies, hierarchical memory), and structured/KG topologies for structured-information integration. It explicitly organizes RAG into 'modular, agentic, and graph-enhanced' architectures.
retriever_type: Survey-level (not one retriever): reviews sparse and dense retrievers, learned retrievers, graph-based retrieval (GraphRAG/HippoRAG), agentic/LLM-driven retrieval (Agentic RAG, Self-RAG, RAG-Gym), and tool retrieval (generative/function-calling). It does not propose a single retriever.
retriever_learning_signal: Survey-level synthesis: surveyed methods span off-the-shelf similarity, contrastive-trained retrievers, LM-feedback/self-reflective retrieval (Self-RAG, CDF-RAG), and RL/agentic retrieval policies (Agentic RAG, RAG-Gym). The survey itself trains nothing; it catalogs these learning signals as design axes rather than reporting one. [uncertain]
query_construction: Survey-level: discusses query forms across methods - raw input queries, decomposed sub-queries (multi-hop / agentic RAG), self-refined/clarified queries, CoT-conditioned queries, and dynamic context assembly. Context Retrieval & Generation includes prompt-based generation and 'Dynamic Assembly' as a way of constructing the context payload. No single query-construction recipe.
query_granularity: Survey-level: spans task-level one-shot retrieval (classic RAG/ICL), iterative/step-level retrieval (agentic and iterative RAG, tool-integrated reasoning per step), and trajectory/session-level memory queries. Presented as a design spectrum, not a fixed choice.
when_to_retrieve: Survey-level: covers one-shot (modular RAG), iterative/agentic (Agentic RAG, RAG-Gym, ReAct-style tool loops), active/adaptive/self-reflective triggering (Self-RAG, CDF-RAG), and memory-driven on-demand retrieval. The survey frames these as the modular->agentic evolution of RAG.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Survey-level: catalogs fixed-schedule retrieval, reflection/self-assessment tokens (Self-RAG), confidence/uncertainty-driven and decision-flow-driven retrieval (CDF-RAG), agent-initiated tool/retrieval requests (function calling, tool-integrated reasoning), and memory recall triggers. Not a single signal; described as an axis of agentic RAG. [uncertain]
reranking: Survey-level: reranking and post-retrieval refinement are discussed as part of modular/advanced RAG and context processing (self-refinement, structured information integration), but the survey does not commit to a single reranker. It treats reranking/refinement as a stage in the RAG pipeline taxonomy.
retrieved_context_refinement: Survey-level: a central theme of 'Context Processing' and 'Context Management' - covers self-refinement (Self-Refine, Reflexion), structured-information integration (StructGPT, KG integration, GraphFormers), context compression (Recurrent Context Compression, Activation Refilling, KV-cache management, Heavy-Hitter Oracle), and long-sequence processing (StreamingLLM, InfLLM, Infini-attention, YaRN). Refinement/compression is one of the survey's three foundational components.
tool_document_engineering: Survey-level: tool-integrated reasoning is a dedicated section (Toolformer, Gorilla, ToolLLM, Granite-Function-Calling, ToRA, ReTool, Chameleon, API-Bank, MCP-RADAR). It discusses tool documentation/description handling and function-calling interfaces, but as a literature survey it does not prescribe a single tool-document-engineering recipe.
index_content_separation: Survey-level: progressive-disclosure / lightweight-index-then-content patterns are implicitly covered under hierarchical memory (MemGPT-style paging between in-context and external store) and context management/compression; the maintained repo (2026 update) adds artifact-backed context and scoped instruction loading. The PDF does not isolate this as a named axis. [uncertain]
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Survey-level: the Multi-Agent Systems and Tool-Integrated Reasoning sections explicitly cover integration protocols - MCP, A2A, ACP, ANP, KQML, FIPA ACL, function-calling - and the maintained repo's 2026 update emphasizes live MCP/A2A/AG-UI protocol coverage and CRUD-style runtime tool/memory management. Static-vs-live tool index is discussed at the ecosystem level, not as one method.
tool_dependency_awareness: Survey-level: inter-tool/multi-tool coordination is named as an evaluation challenge ('Multi-Tool Coordination', MCP-RADAR; nested tools NesTools, ToolHop) and orchestration is covered in multi-agent systems, but the survey does not propose a specific dependency-graph mechanism. [uncertain]
how_retrieved_used: Survey-level: covers the full spectrum - prompt augmentation (RAG, ICL), context assembly/formatting into the payload, self-refinement feeding back into generation, memory injection for persistence, tool outputs fed back into reasoning (tool-integrated reasoning), and orchestration across agents. The unifying view is that all of these populate/optimize the inference-time context C.
planning_integration: Survey-level: planning/acting integration is covered via Tool-Integrated Reasoning (ReAct, Program-Aided Language Models, ToRA, Chameleon - interleaved reason-act-retrieve loops), Agentic RAG (retrieve-within-a-loop, RAG-Gym), and Multi-Agent orchestration/coordination (MetaGPT, AutoGen, CAMEL, CrewAI, CoA, SagaLLM). It catalogs per-step interleaved, plan-then-act, and orchestrated multi-agent integration patterns.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Survey-level: spans per-answer (single-shot RAG), per-CoT-step (CoT/ToT/GoT, iterative retrieval), and per-tool-call within a rollout (ReAct, tool-integrated reasoning). Presented as the modular->agentic spectrum rather than a fixed granularity.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (the survey itself adapts no retrieved case). At the catalog level it discusses self-refinement (Self-Refine, Reflexion) and agentic revision as adaptation strategies of surveyed systems, but adaptation_mechanism is a per-method CBR property not applicable to a survey. [N/A]
retrieved_item_representation: Survey-level: covers raw documents/snippets, structured/KG representations (StructGPT, GraphFormers, KG integration), distilled/compressed context (context compression, summarization), workflow/agent memory entries, and tool/function specifications. Surface form varies by surveyed system; no single representation.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Survey-level: ranges from concrete documents/demonstrations (RAG, ICL) to structured knowledge subgraphs (GraphRAG/KG), compressed/distilled context (context management), persistent memory abstractions (memory hierarchies), and tool/skill abstractions (tool-integrated reasoning). Multi-level by design.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Survey-level: discusses self-reflection / self-refinement (Self-RAG, Self-Refine, Reflexion), contextual calibration, brittleness assessment, corrective/decision-flow RAG (CDF-RAG), and context-handling-failure analysis as robustness themes; it analyzes these as challenges (e.g. 'Context Handling Failures', 'Brittleness Assessment') rather than proposing one mechanism.
memory_type: Survey-level: a full dedicated 'Memory Systems' section covering episodic/long-term memory, memory hierarchies, and procedural/persistent memory (MemoryBank, MemGPT, MemOS, A-MEM, Self-Controlled Memory, REMEMBERER, Short-term & Long-term memory, Memory-Enhanced Agents). Also covers graph and latent memory under structured integration. The survey treats all memory types as a taxonomy, not a single type.
write_back: Survey-level: True as a covered theme - the Memory Systems section centers on writing/storing experiences for persistent interactions (MemoryBank, MemGPT paging, A-MEM agentic memory, REMEMBERER). The survey itself stores nothing; it catalogs write-back as a memory-system capability.
online_growth: Survey-level: Yes as a covered theme - persistent, growing agent memory during deployment is a defining property of the Memory Systems section (and the repo's 2026 'runtime memory / project memory' update). Not a property of the survey artifact itself.
write_back_trigger: Survey-level: covered as an axis of memory systems (on-interaction writes, reflective/self-controlled writes, scheduled consolidation in memory hierarchies). The survey does not report a single write-back trigger; it catalogs them across MemoryBank/MemGPT/A-MEM/Self-Controlled Memory. [uncertain]
failure_experience_usage: Survey-level: discussed via self-refinement/reflection methods that learn from failed attempts (Reflexion, self-correction) and corrective RAG; not a property the survey itself implements. [uncertain]
memory_evolution_update: Survey-level: covered as memory management - append, consolidation/compression, hierarchical paging (MemGPT/MemOS), agentic linking/evolution (A-MEM 'agentic memory' linking and evolving notes). The survey catalogs these update dynamics rather than committing to one.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Survey-level: covered - agentic/RL-driven retrieval and decision policies are reviewed (Agentic RAG, RAG-Gym, Self-RAG's learned reflection, RL for tool/retrieval decisions), contrasted with fixed similarity top-k modular RAG. The survey presents learned-policy retrieval as the agentic end of the RAG spectrum, not its own contribution.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Survey-level: a dedicated 'Multi-Agent Systems' section covers cross-agent communication, shared context/memory, orchestration, and interoperability protocols (KQML, FIPA ACL, MCP, A2A, ACP, ANP; AutoGen, MetaGPT, CAMEL, CrewAI, Swarm, SagaLLM, CoA). Cross-agent/cross-framework context sharing is explicitly treated as a first-class concern.
benchmarks: The survey's Evaluation section catalogs many benchmarks (it does not run experiments). Named examples include GAIA, GTA, WebArena, VideoWebArena, Deep Research Bench, StableToolBench, NesTools, ToolHop, T-Eval, BFCL (Berkeley Function-Calling Leaderboard), NarrativeQA, MEMENTO, API-Bank, Mind2Web, SWE-Bench, LongMemEval, MADail-Bench, MCP-RADAR.
benchmark_family: Survey-wide coverage across families: agentic/general (GAIA, GTA, Deep Research Bench), web (WebArena, VideoWebArena, Mind2Web), tool/function-calling (StableToolBench, NesTools, ToolHop, T-Eval, BFCL, API-Bank, MCP-RADAR), memory (LongMemEval, MEMENTO, MADail-Bench), QA/long-context (NarrativeQA), and code (SWE-Bench). It is a multi-family catalog, not a single benchmark family.
baselines: N/A. As a survey it reports no head-to-head baselines or new experimental comparisons; it reviews and contrasts methods qualitatively rather than benchmarking a proposed system against baselines.
key_metrics: N/A as own results. The survey discusses, at the meta level, the metrics used across the field (task success/pass rate, accuracy, tool-call correctness, retrieval/answer quality, memory recall over long horizons) and critiques evaluation; it reports no metric numbers of its own.
headline_result: No quantitative headline number (survey, not a method). The qualitative headline finding: across 1400+ analyzed papers, a fundamental asymmetry exists - LLMs augmented by advanced context engineering are highly proficient at UNDERSTANDING complex contexts but exhibit pronounced limitations in GENERATING equally sophisticated, long-form outputs; closing this comprehension-generation gap is named the defining future priority.
ablations: N/A. A survey performs no ablation studies. (Its analytical equivalent is the decomposition into Foundational Components vs System Implementations and the identification of the comprehension-generation asymmetry and evaluation challenges.)
evaluation_decoupling: Survey-level: it explicitly distinguishes Component-Level Assessment from System-Level Integration evaluation (Evaluation Frameworks section), i.e. it argues for decoupling intrinsic component metrics from end-to-end system metrics, and flags 'Memory System Isolation Problems' as an evaluation challenge. It does not itself report intrinsic-vs-end-to-end numbers.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Survey-level: discusses both, advocating beyond outcome-only scoring - it raises process-oriented concerns (reasoning faithfulness, multi-tool coordination, transactional integrity, self-validation dependencies, attribution challenges) alongside final-task outcome metrics, as part of its Evaluation Challenges.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Survey-level: a recurring theme via Context Management/Processing - O(n^2) attention scaling limitations, context compression, KV-cache management (Heavy-Hitter Oracle, StreamingLLM), and efficient long-context methods (Mamba/LongNet/FlashAttention/Infini-attention) are reviewed as cost-vs-capability tradeoffs. No single cost/accuracy number is reported. [uncertain]
context_budget_and_selection_count: Survey-level: formalized in the definition - context payload C is optimized subject to a length budget |C| <= L_max, motivating compression, selection, and management; specific k/budget choices are method-dependent and not fixed by the survey. [uncertain]
survey_scope_and_axes: Organizing axes (Figure 1 taxonomy): (A) Foundational Components - (4.1) Context Retrieval & Generation, (4.2) Context Processing, (4.3) Context Management; (B) System Implementations - (5.1) Retrieval-Augmented Generation (modular / agentic / graph-enhanced), (5.2) Memory Systems, (5.3) Tool-Integrated Reasoning, (5.4) Multi-Agent Systems; plus (6) Evaluation (frameworks, benchmark datasets, challenges) and (7) Future Directions (foundational research, technical innovation, application-driven). Coverage: 'over 1400 research papers' analyzed; 166 pages; 1411 citations/references in the bibliography; evolution timeline spans 2020-2025 (maintained repo extended to ~March 2026).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A. The survey introduces no new benchmark/dataset of its own; it reviews and categorizes existing ones (see benchmarks/benchmark_family). [N/A]
builds_on: Positions itself relative to and builds upon prior vertical surveys it cites: prompt-engineering surveys, knowledge-graph/structured-knowledge-integration surveys, long-context surveys, RAG surveys (including modular/agentic/graph-enhanced RAG surveys), LLM-agent surveys, tool-learning/function-calling surveys, and multi-agent-systems surveys. Conceptually builds on the autoregressive LLM probabilistic model to define context optimization.
contrasts_with: Explicitly contrasts itself with (a) 'prompt engineering' as too narrow (a single static string) and (b) prior surveys that treat individual verticals (RAG, memory, tool use, multi-agent, long context) in isolation; its differentiator is a horizontal, unifying taxonomy that separates foundational components from their integration into systems and surfaces the cross-domain connections those vertical surveys leave implicit.
lineage: Surveys group: a unifying meta-survey of the retrieval-/context-augmented LLM landscape. It sits above and stitches together the per-topic lineages (ICL/demonstration retrieval, RAG and agentic/graph RAG, agent memory, tool retrieval/use, multi-agent orchestration), providing the umbrella 'Context Engineering' framework under which the other works in this collection (RAG, memory, tool, CBR, multi-agent methods) can be located.
